def: Power itself — the Goddess as the active energy of consciousness that makes, keeps and melts the world.
The measuring-out power: makes the One look like many; also the Mother's own magic of illusion.
The Absolute — boundless being-consciousness-bliss underneath everything.
Pure awareness — the light by which everything is known.
Bliss — not fun but the fullness of being, sought in every desire.
A sound-form of the deity — chanted to wake Her presence; e.g. the nine-lettered navārṇa.
The nine-lettered Goddess mantra (Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce) — speech, power and desire seeds in one.
Armour-hymn — posts a goddess-guard on every limb and direction.
Steady picturing — holding the deity's form in the heart till mind melts into it.
Repeated chanting — turning the mantra with breath and bead till it chants itself.
Worship with offerings — flowers, lamp, food and love given to the deity.
The teacher — dispeller of darkness; grace flows guru-to-pupil, heart to heart.
Loving devotion — clinging to the Mother as a child clings, till love itself frees.
Knowing — first book-learning, finally direct seeing that 'I am That'.
Freedom — release from birth-and-death round; living it now is jīvanmukti.
Action and its fruit-seed — every deed ripens; selfless work purifies the doer.
I-maker — the knot that says 'I, mine'; loosened by devotion and wisdom.
The Heart — in Trika, the pulsing oneness of Śiva and Śakti, not the body-organ.
The Beyond-which-nothing — Trika's name for the Absolute past all levels.
Emission — consciousness endlessly pouring itself out, yet resting in itself.
Family — the clan of energies, the body, the lineage; Trika's home-word for the whole.
The Triad — Śiva, Śakti and the bound soul; or will, wisdom, action — three made one.
Means — Śāmbhava (will), Śākta (wisdom), Āṇava (action-breath-body) paths to the same goal.
Initiation — the teacher plants awakened consciousness in the pupil.
